content.value_statement: Swift concurrency changes can create data races, actor isolation errors, and migration uncertainty. This skill guides safe async/await, actors, Sendable, testing, and Swift 6 migration decisions.
actual_capabilities: Explains async/await, async let, task groups, cancellation, and structured concurrency choices.
Guides actor isolation, @MainActor usage, nonisolated APIs, and reentrancy risks.
Helps resolve Sendable diagnostics and data race warnings during Swift 6 migration.
Covers Core Data, testing, memory management, and performance patterns for concurrent Swift code.
Provides triage steps for common compiler errors and project setting checks.
limitations: Does not run Swift builds or tests by itself.
Requires project settings when advice depends on Swift language mode or toolchain behavior.
May need your code context to choose between actors, @MainActor, and value types.
Course links are supplemental and are not required for normal use.

use_cases.title: Fix Actor Isolation Errors
use_cases.description: Diagnose MainActor, nonisolated, actor instance, and custom actor boundary problems in Swift code.

use_cases.title: Plan Swift 6 Migration
use_cases.description: Break migration work into small changes with build setting checks and verification steps.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Async Tests
use_cases.description: Improve XCTest and Swift Testing patterns for async work, cancellation, and deterministic state checks.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Diagnostic
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner needs help understanding a compiler message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this Swift Concurrency diagnostic in simple terms. Tell me what isolation boundary is involved and the safest first fix.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Tool
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer is starting a new asynchronous feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am adding asynchronous work to a Swift feature. Help me choose between async/await, async let, Task, TaskGroup, and actor isolation.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer has existing code with possible data race risk.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Swift code for data race risks. Recommend small changes using actors, @MainActor, Sendable, or structured tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Team is preparing a Swift 6 concurrency migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Swift 6 concurrency migration plan for this module. Include build settings to confirm, risky APIs, verification steps, and rollback notes.

output_examples.input: A view model update triggers MainActor diagnostics after enabling Swift 6.
output: Identifies the UI isolation boundary and why the diagnostic appears.
Compares targeted MainActor isolation with broader type isolation.
Lists checks for default actor isolation and strict concurrency settings.

output_examples.input: A test checks loading state around an async fetch and fails intermittently.
output: Explains why task scheduling makes the assertion unreliable.
Suggests deterministic async testing patterns and main serial execution.
Adds verification steps for cancellation and final state.

output_examples.input: Core Data objects cause Sendable warnings when passed across tasks.
output: Recommends passing object identifiers or immutable data transfer values.
Explains why managed objects should stay within their context boundary.
Suggests background context patterns and merge verification.

best_practices: Confirm Swift language mode, strict concurrency level, and default actor isolation before giving migration advice.
Prefer structured concurrency, explicit isolation, and small refactors that can be reviewed and tested.
Use unsafe annotations only with documented invariants and a plan to remove them.
anti_patterns: Do not add @MainActor everywhere without proving the state belongs on the main actor.
Do not pass non-Sendable reference types across isolation boundaries without a safe design.
Do not block async code with semaphores, sleeps, or thread-centric assumptions.

faq.question: Can this skill fix Swift Concurrency compiler errors?
faq.answer: It can explain likely causes and propose changes. You still need to apply and test the code.

faq.question: Does it support Swift 6 migration work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes migration strategy, strict concurrency checks, Sendable issues, and verification guidance.

faq.question: Can it choose between actors and @MainActor?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for the isolation boundary and recommends the narrowest correct model for the code.

faq.question: Does it include Core Data guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers managed object isolation, object identifiers, background contexts, and default isolation conflicts.

faq.question: Will it run project commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides guidance and verification steps. Command execution depends on the host agent and user approval.

faq.question: Are the external course links required?
faq.answer: No. They are optional learning references. The skill includes the practical guidance needed for normal use.
